diagnostic_evidence.quote: the orthogonal Tucker factor matrices $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} \in \R^{n_\ell \times r_\ell^0}$
$G^{(\ell)}\in \mathbb{R}^{r_\ell\times r_\ell^0}$
is the set of orthonormal vectors for $\ell = 1, \cdots, d$.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity asserted in the proof is false: $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}[G^{(\ell)}]^T[V^{(\ell)}]^T$ is $n_\ell\times n_\ell$ of rank at most $r^0_\ell$, so it cannot equal $I_{n_\ell}$. The statement actually needed is $(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})^T(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})=[G^{(\ell)}]^TG^{(\ell)}=I_{r^0_\ell}$, which requires $G^{(\ell)}$ to have orthonormal columns. That is implied only if the phrase "orthogonal Tucker tensor" is read through the orthonormality convention of (2.3); Definition def:hybridTuck_form (B), the two-level format the proposition converts, places no such condition on $G^{(\ell)}$. Hence the conclusion that $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}$ are orthogonal Tucker factor matrices is not established for the format as defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted identity by $(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})^T(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})=I_{r^0_\ell}$ and impose (or note as w.l.o.g. via $G\mapsto G(G^TG)^{-1/2}$, $\beta^0\mapsto\beta^0\times(G^TG)^{1/2}$) orthonormal columns of $G^{(\ell)}$ in Definition def:hybridTuck_form.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality part of the conclusion of prop:hybrid2Tuck, and any claim that the two-level hybrid format is an orthogonal Tucker representation (e.g. the advertised "two-level orthogonal algebraic Tucker tensor"), are unreliable; the algebraic rank-reduction identity (2.15) is unaffected.
issues.title: False orthogonality identity in the two-level to Tucker conversion
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the orthogonalization of $G^{(\ell)}$ is free of cost and loses no generality, so the rank-reduction conclusion and all guarantees survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The orthogonality property is based on the argument analogues to the  algebraic case but reformulated for polynomial arrays and note that the inner product should be properly weighted.
which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$.
where the Tucker factor functions are given by $v^{(\ell)}(x_\ell) = T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell) V^{(\ell)} \in \R^{r_\ell}$

issues.failure_explanation: With $v_j(x)=\sum_i V_{ij}T_{i-1}(x)$ and Euclidean-orthonormal columns of $V$, orthogonality in the Chebyshev-weighted inner product (the one in which the $T_k$ are orthogonal) holds iff $V^T\Gamma V=I$ with $\Gamma=\mathrm{diag}(\pi,\pi/2,\ldots)$; this is not implied by $V^TV=I$. Counterexample: $m_\ell=3$, $v_{1,2}=(T_0\pm T_1)/\sqrt2$ give $\langle v_1,v_2\rangle_w=(\pi-\pi/2)/2=\pi/4\neq0$. The proof offers only a hand-wave about a "properly weighted" inner product. In addition, $T_{0:m_\ell-1}V^{(\ell)}$ has $r_\ell$ entries, not $r^0_\ell$ as claimed.

failure_location.quote: If \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker} present the orthogonal Tucker tensor, then $\{T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell)V^{(\ell)}\}$ appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either require weighted orthonormality $V^{(\ell)T}\Gamma V^{(\ell)}=I$ (absorbing $\Gamma^{1/2}$ into the factors), or delete the orthogonality sentence and correct the stated number of polynomials.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted orthogonality of the ChebTuck factor polynomials is false/unsupported as stated; the representation identity eqn:cheb_func_tuck (and Proposition prop:funcTuck's first conclusion) is unaffected.
issues.title: Unsupported orthogonality claim for the functional Tucker factor polynomials
issues.why_classification: A short local fix (strengthened normalization or deletion of the side claim) preserves the proposition's substantive content; no downstream result uses the orthogonality assertion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\| \boldsymbol{\xi} \|_1 = \sum_{k=1}^{R} |\xi_k|$ is the $\ell_1$ norm of the normalization constants.
\xi_k \in \mathbb{R},

issues.failure_explanation: Every intermediate bound carries $\xi_k$ instead of $|\xi_k|$. Since the CP weights are real and may be negative, the displayed bound has a right-hand side that can be negative while the left-hand side is nonnegative (e.g. $R=1$, $\xi_1=-1$), so the statement is false as written, and the proof step $|\sum_k\xi_k(\cdot)|\leq\sum_k\xi_k|(\cdot)|$ is an invalid triangle inequality. The final display then silently replaces $\sum_k\xi_k$ by $\|\boldsymbol\xi\|_1=\sum_k|\xi_k|$, which does not follow from the preceding line.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert $|\xi_k|$ in the statement and in each inequality of the proof (and fix the stray $R_L$ summation limit).
issues.overall_effect: The first bound of lem:ftilde-F and the proof chain leading to (4.20) are invalid for signed CP weights; the "in particular" bound with $\|\boldsymbol\xi\|_1$ used in thm:added-1 becomes correct once the absolute values are restored.
issues.title: Missing absolute values on the CP weights in the interpolation error lemma
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced and local; after it, every claim, including the bound used in thm:added-1, holds unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The desired result then follows from the standard error analysis of the RHOSVD truncation \cite[Theorem 2.5]{khoromskij2009multigrid}.
the singular values $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ are available after the SVD decomposition of the side matrices in the CP format
{\bf C} = {\bf T} \times_1 W^{(1)} \times_2 W^{(2)} \times_3 W^{(3)} = \sum_{k=1}^{R}\xi_k {\bf c}_k^{(1)} \otimes {\bf c}_k^{(2)} \otimes {\bf c}_k^{(3)},
\| \tilde{f}_{\bf m} - \hat{f}_{\bf m} \|_{\infty} \leq \sqrt{m_1 m_2 m_3} \| {\bf C} - \hat{\bf{C}} \|_{\mathrm{F}}.

issues.failure_explanation: The quantities $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ are never defined in the lemma; the only interpretation given (singular values of the CP side matrices) makes the estimate false. For ${\bf C}=\sum_k\xi_k c^{(1)}_k\otimes c^{(2)}_k\otimes c^{(3)}_k$ the mode-$\ell$ unfolding is $\Phi^{(\ell)}\mathrm{diag}(\xi)(\Phi^{(j)}\odot\Phi^{(k)})^T$, so its singular values carry the additional Khatri-Rao factor $\|\Phi^{(j)}\odot\Phi^{(k)}\|_2$, which the bound omits. Decisively, the right-hand side is not invariant under the rescaling freedom $c^{(\ell)}_k\mapsto\lambda^{(\ell)}_kc^{(\ell)}_k$, $\xi_k\mapsto\xi_k/\prod_\ell\lambda^{(\ell)}_k$ of the same tensor ${\bf C}$ (the left-hand side is), so it can be driven to zero while the error stays fixed. Explicitly, for $R=2$, $\xi=(1,-1)$, $c^{(1)}=(u,u+\epsilon v)$, $c^{(2)}=c^{(3)}=L(u,u+\epsilon v)$ and $r=(1,1,1)$, the truncation error is $\Theta(L^2\epsilon)$ whereas the stated bound is $O(L\epsilon)$. If instead $\sigma^{(\ell)}$ denoted unfolding singular values, the extra factor $\|\boldsymbol\xi\|$ destroys homogeneity and the computability claim in the remark fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the estimate in terms of quantities that scale correctly with the CP representation, e.g. bound the mode-$\ell$ tail by $\sigma_{r_\ell+1}(\Phi^{\ell})\|(\Phi^{(j)}\odot\Phi^{(k)})\mathrm{diag}(\xi)\|$, or normalize the canonical vectors and absorb their norms into $\boldsymbol\xi$, and define $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The second (RHOSVD) term of the error guarantee in thm:added-1 is unreliable, so the advertised computable accuracy certificate for the CP-input ChebTuck approximation is unsupported in general; the first term (lem:ftilde-F) is unaffected.
issues.title: RHOSVD error bound omits cross-mode factor norms
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a corrected estimate (extra cross-mode factors or a normalization hypothesis plus redefined singular values) and changes the stated error guarantee, but the RHOSVD-based algorithm and a comparable a posteriori bound survive without new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.
\Require Given a tensor ${\bf F}\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1 \times n_2 \times n_3}$ discretizing function $f: [-1,1]^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the uniform grid
\State Construct the multivariate cubic spline interpolation $Q(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ of the data ${\bf F}$ on the uniform grid by, e.g., \texttt{interpn} in MATLAB.

issues.failure_explanation: alg:cheb_tuck_alg must read and process the full $n_1\times n_2\times n_3$ input tensor to build the trivariate spline; constructing the spline coefficients costs $\Omega(n^3)$ (mode-wise tridiagonal solves on $n^3$ data), while the claimed cost $C_4m^3(m+n)$ is only $O(m^3n)$ in the regime $m\ll n$ that the paper advertises ($|r|\ll m\ll O(h^{-1})$). The bound is exceeded whenever $n>m^{3/2}$, e.g. $m=129$, $n=4096$ as in the paper's own experiments. The 1D argument ($O(n)$ tridiagonal solve plus $O(m)$ evaluation) cannot be extended by multiplying the whole $O(m+n)$ by the $m^3$ evaluation points.

failure_location.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg}: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the spline-construction term $O(n^3)$ (or $O(n^3+m^3+mn^2+m^2n)$ for a tensor-product spline with tensor-grid evaluation) to the estimate for alg:cheb_tuck_alg.
issues.overall_effect: The stated complexity of alg:cheb_tuck_alg understates its true cost (and its memory traffic) in the intended regime; the estimates for the other three algorithms are unaffected.
issues.title: Complexity of the trivariate spline step understates the input-size cost
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing cost term is a local correction that keeps the form of the complexity statement and all accuracy guarantees; no algorithm or proof must be redesigned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the Tucker rank $r = \mathcal{O}(|\log \varepsilon|)$ is assumed
and the cost of reconstruction of the Tucker core tensor $\boldsymbol{\beta}$, which is $\mathcal{O}(R r^3)$

issues.failure_explanation: All four complexity formulas express the tolerance dependence through $|\log\varepsilon|$ (e.g. $C_3m^4|\log\varepsilon|$ and $C_{11}R|\log\varepsilon|^3$), which is obtained only by substituting $r=O(|\log\varepsilon|)$ into the actual costs $O(m^4r)$ and $O(Rr^3)$. The proof declares this as an assumption, but the proposition asserts the bounds unconditionally. For inputs whose multilinear ranks decay slowly (e.g. algebraically in $\varepsilon$) the rank can far exceed $|\log\varepsilon|$ and the stated costs are wrong.

failure_location.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_func}: $C_{f} m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the required Tucker ranks satisfy $r=O(|\log\varepsilon|)$ (equivalently, exponentially decaying unfolding singular values) to the statement of prop:compl, and state the bounds with $r$ otherwise.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised complexity guarantees hold only for functions/tensors with exponentially decaying multilinear ranks (e.g. the Newton-kernel class), not for the general inputs the proposition quantifies over.
issues.title: Complexity bounds silently assume rank O(|log eps|)
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard rank-decay condition is a one-clause local repair that preserves the method, the rates and the scope the source itself claims ("a wide range of functions").
